paragraphs: The American country singer Garth Brooks will play 11 concerts on the island of Ireland next summer. Tickets went on sale on Thursday and sold very fast.
The concerts are in Galway, Kilkenny, Limerick, Cork and Belfast. Many fans now need a place to stay.
Hotel prices went up very quickly. In Galway, almost all rooms were gone by 9.30am. One apartment cost €2,700 for one night. In Kilkenny, only one place was left, and it was in another county.
The head of a group for Irish hotels said hotels are not being unfair. He said prices go up and down with demand. He was happy that the concerts are outside Dublin.
sentZh: 美國鄉村歌手葛斯·布魯克斯明年夏天將在愛爾蘭島舉行11場演唱會。
門票週四開賣，賣得非常快。
演唱會在高威、基爾肯尼、利默里克、科克和貝爾法斯特舉行。
許多歌迷現在需要住宿的地方。
飯店價格很快就漲了。
在高威，早上九點半前幾乎所有房間都沒了。
一間公寓一晚要價2700歐元。
在基爾肯尼只剩一個住處，而且在另一個郡。
一個愛爾蘭飯店團體的負責人說飯店並沒有不公平。
他說價格隨需求上下波動。
他很高興演唱會辦在都柏林以外的地方。

paragraphs: Tickets for Garth Brooks's concerts in Ireland next summer sold quickly on Thursday. The American country star will now play 11 shows, after a third night was added in Belfast because so many people wanted tickets.
The concerts will take place in Galway, Kilkenny, Limerick, Cork and Belfast. As soon as tickets went on sale, the price of hotel rooms in these places rose sharply.

By 9.30am, up to 98% of places to stay in Galway were not available on the concert dates. One apartment 21km from the city was listed at €2,700 for a night. In Limerick, a double room was €353, and for the Kilkenny show, only one cottage in County Carlow was left.

Paul Gallagher of the Irish Hotels Federation said hotels change their prices depending on demand. He said hotel prices have only risen by a little over 1% this year. He also said it was good that the concerts would bring tourists to areas outside Dublin.
sentZh: 葛斯·布魯克斯明年夏天在愛爾蘭的演唱會門票週四迅速售出。
由於想買票的人太多，貝爾法斯特加開第三晚，這位美國鄉村巨星現在將演出11場。
演唱會將在高威、基爾肯尼、利默里克、科克和貝爾法斯特舉行。
門票一開賣，這些地方的飯店房價就急劇上漲。
到早上九點半，高威在演唱會日期有高達98%的住處已無法預訂。
一間距離市區21公里的公寓標價一晚2700歐元。
在利默里克，一間雙人房要353歐元；基爾肯尼那場則只剩下卡洛郡的一間小屋。
愛爾蘭飯店協會的保羅·加拉格說，飯店會依需求調整價格。
他說今年飯店價格只上漲略多於1%。
他也說演唱會能把遊客帶到都柏林以外的地區是件好事。

paragraphs: Hotel prices surged on Thursday as tickets for Garth Brooks's Irish tour next summer sold rapidly. Because of high demand, the American country singer added a third night in Belfast, bringing the total number of concerts to 11.
The shows will be held in Galway, Kilkenny, Limerick, Cork and Belfast, rather than in Dublin. Within hours, accommodation near the venues became scarce and expensive.

By 9.30am, booking websites showed that up to 98% of properties in Galway were unavailable on the concert dates, with one apartment 21km away advertised at €2,700 for a night. In Limerick, 94% of listings had gone, while rooms in Cork city centre cost between €400 and €500. However, owners may still release more rooms later.

Paul Gallagher, chief executive of the Irish Hotels Federation, rejected claims of price gouging and said hotels use dynamic pricing based on demand. He pointed out that January rates are about half of those in July and August.
He also welcomed the decision to hold the concerts outside the capital, saying it would spread tourism to the regions.
sentZh: 週四，葛斯·布魯克斯明年夏天愛爾蘭巡演的門票迅速售出，飯店價格隨之飆漲。
由於需求旺盛，這位美國鄉村歌手在貝爾法斯特加開第三晚，使演唱會總數達到11場。
演出將在高威、基爾肯尼、利默里克、科克和貝爾法斯特舉行，而不是在都柏林。
幾小時內，場館附近的住宿就變得稀少又昂貴。
到早上九點半，訂房網站顯示高威在演唱會日期有高達98%的房源無法預訂，一間21公里外的公寓一晚標價2700歐元。
在利默里克，94%的房源已被訂走，而科克市中心的房間要價400至500歐元。
不過，屋主之後仍可能釋出更多房間。

他指出，一月的房價約為七、八月的一半。
他也歡迎在首都以外舉辦演唱會的決定，表示這能把觀光帶到各地區。

paragraphs: Accommodation prices skyrocketed on Thursday as tickets for Garth Brooks's Irish tour, scheduled for next summer, were snapped up within hours. Overwhelming demand prompted the country music star to tack on a third Belfast date, taking the tally to 11 concerts.
Notably, the shows bypass Dublin altogether, with Galway, Kilkenny, Limerick, Cork and Belfast playing host instead. Rooms in these locations promptly became both scarce and exorbitantly priced.

By mid-morning, booking platforms indicated that up to 98% of properties in Galway were unavailable, and one apartment 21km from the city commanded €2,700 for a single night. Limerick had been all but cleared out, and city-centre rooms in Cork fetched between €400 and €500. Nonetheless, such listings offer only a partial snapshot, since owners may release further rooms.

Paul Gallagher, chief executive of the Irish Hotels Federation, bluntly dismissed accusations of price gouging, attributing the spikes to dynamic pricing. He noted that January rates are roughly half those of high summer and that hotel price inflation this year has been barely above 1%.
He also applauded the promoter's choice of regional venues, arguing that it would disperse tourist spending beyond the capital.
